what_its_for: This eye drop or eye ointment is used to treat eye infections caused by bacteria and to reduce swelling, redness, and irritation in the eye at the same time. It contains two medicines: tobramycin (an antibiotic that kills bacteria) and dexamethasone (a steroid that reduces inflammation).
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before and after using this medicine. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket, and gently squeeze the prescribed number of drops into the pocket — do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, eyelid, or any surface. If using the ointment, pull down your lower eyelid and squeeze a small ribbon of ointment inside the lid. Close your eye gently and blink a few times. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each medicine. If using both drops and ointment, use the drops first and wait at least 10 minutes before applying the ointment. Remove contact lenses before use and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in.
dosing: For eye drops: The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye(s) every 4 to 6 hours. During the first day or two, your doctor may ask you to use it more often, such as every 2 hours while awake. For eye ointment: Apply a small amount (about half an inch) to the affected eye(s) 3 to 4 times a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different depending on how severe your condition is.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or use extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store eye drops and ointment at room temperature, between 46°F and 80°F (8°C and 27°C). Do not freeze. Keep the bottle or tube tightly closed when not in use. Throw away the drops or ointment after the number of days recommended by your doctor or pharmacist after opening — typically within 28 days. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not touch the dropper tip or tube tip to your eye, fingers, or any other surface, as this can contaminate the medicine and cause a new infection. Do not wear contact lenses while your eye is infected or while you are being treated, unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid driving or doing activities that require clear vision right after using this medicine, as it may cause temporary blurred vision. Do not use this medicine longer than your doctor prescribed, even if your symptoms improve, because overuse of the steroid ingredient can lead to serious eye problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: worsening redness, pain, or swelling of the eye; vision changes or sudden vision loss; increased sensitivity to light; eye discharge that gets worse; signs of a new or worsening eye infection; severe eye irritation or burning that does not go away; or if your symptoms do not start improving after a few days of use. Long-term use of steroid eye drops can raise the pressure inside your eye (glaucoma) or cause cataracts, so let your doctor know if you experience eye pain or pressure.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement in redness, swelling, and discomfort within 1 to 2 days of starting treatment. The full course of treatment usually lasts 7 to 10 days. It is very important to use all of the medicine for as long as your doctor told you to, even if you start feeling better sooner. Stopping too early may allow the infection to come back.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this combination in pregnancy has not been fully established. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but your doctor will determine if it is appropriate and what dose is safe for your child. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is typically needed, but older adults should be monitored for signs of increased eye pressure with prolonged use. People with certain eye conditions: Do not use this medicine if you have a viral eye infection (such as herpes), a fungal eye infection, or certain other eye diseases unless your doctor specifically prescribes it, as the steroid ingredient can make those conditions much worse.
